description: A customer's excess is their share minus the average share.

b.request: Sum each customer’s invoice totals, divide each customer’s total by overall revenue to get their share, and calculate the average share across all customers; for customers whose share is above that average, return one row containing their average total spent, average share, and average of (customer share minus average share), without rounding
b.sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_spent FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), shares AS (SELECT CustomerId, total_spent, total_spent * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(total_spent) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM customer_totals), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM shares) SELECT AVG(s.total_spent) AS average_total_spent, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.value) AS average_share_above_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN average_share a WHERE s.share > a.value;

c.request: Total up each customer's invoice totals and work out each customer's share of overall revenue (their total over the sum across all customers). Keep the customers whose share is above the average share. Give one row with: the average amount those customers spent, their average share, and on average how much their share beats the average share. No rounding. A customer's excess is their share minus the average share.
c.sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS amount_spent FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), customer_shares AS (SELECT amount_spent, amount_spent * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(amount_spent) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM customer_totals), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM customer_shares) SELECT AVG(cs.amount_spent) AS average_amount_spent, AVG(cs.share) AS average_share, AVG(cs.share - a.value) AS average_excess_share FROM customer_shares AS cs CROSS JOIN average_share AS a WHERE cs.share > a.value;

a.request: Total up each customer's invoice `Total`s, and compute each customer's share of overall revenue (their total divided by the sum over all customers). Find the average share across customers, and keep the customers whose share is above it. Return one row with: the average total spent by those customers, their average share, and the average difference between their share and the average share (share minus average share). Don't round.
a.sql: WITH customer_totals AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_spent FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), customer_shares AS (SELECT total_spent, total_spent * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(total_spent) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM customer_totals), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM customer_shares) SELECT AVG(cs.total_spent) AS average_total_spent, AVG(cs.share) AS average_share, AVG(cs.share - a.value) AS average_share_difference FROM customer_shares cs CROSS JOIN average_share a WHERE cs.share > a.value;

d.request: For each customer, sum their invoice totals and divide by total revenue across all customers to find their revenue share. Keep customers whose share is above the average customer share. Return one row containing their average total spend, their average share, and their average excess, where each customer’s excess is their share minus the average share. Do not round.
d.sql: WITH customer_spend AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_spend FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), customer_share AS (SELECT total_spend, total_spend * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(total_spend) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM customer_spend), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share FROM customer_share) SELECT AVG(total_spend) AS average_total_spend, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - benchmark.average_share) AS average_excess FROM customer_share CROSS JOIN benchmark WHERE share > benchmark.average_share
